title: Cobalt‐based water oxidation electrocatalyst to assist the oxygen evolution reaction as an energy conversion system
content:
Abstract

A high-performance oxygen evolution electrocatalyst is synthesized based on Graphite electrode modification by Hydroxylammonium|Cobalt nanoparticles to assist the water oxidation reaction as a renewable energy system. Cyclic voltammetry, linear sweep voltammetry, and chronoamperometry were used to determine the electrocatalyst performance. According to the resulted electrochemical parameters, the electron transfer coefficient was equal to 0.81, the electron transfer rate constant was equal to 3.16 s−1, and the saturated adsorptive capacity of the electroactive substance at the electrode surface was equal to 8.06 × 10−8 mol cm−2. The low overpotential in an alkaline solution, the high electrochemically active surface area equal to 0.048 mm2, and the small Tafel slope equal to 59.5 mV dec−1, which was superior to that of other cobalt-based electrocatalysts, indicates the high-speed kinetics, confirming the ability of this electrocatalyst in the electrochemical water oxidation reaction as an energy conversion system.
